definition: In a showy way that is meant to attract attention or impress other people.
example: He ostentatiously checked his new gold watch every few minutes during dinner.
nuance: Conspicuously means only "noticeably," but ostentatiously suggests a deliberate wish to be seen and admired.
prompt: A guest arrives at a neighbor's casual backyard barbecue.
options: Priya ostentatiously jangled her gold bracelets whenever someone glanced her way.
Hoping no one would notice her late arrival, the guest ostentatiously slipped in through the side gate.
She ostentatiously came to help cook, but she really just wanted free burgers.
The guest ostentatiously sneezed twice because of the pollen in the yard.
reasons: Making her jewelry jingle on purpose so people notice it is a showy bid for attention.
Trying to go unseen is the reverse of showing off.
This confuses the word with ostensibly, which means "seemingly" or "supposedly."
An involuntary sneeze is not a deliberate effort to impress anyone.

practice.prompt: A student gets the highest score in the class on a math exam.
options: After weeks of practice, Marcus ostentatiously understood every formula on the test.
Marcus ostentatiously waved his graded test over his head as he walked to his seat.
Without a word, Marcus ostentatiously folded the test and tucked it into his backpack.
Marcus ostentatiously thanked his tutor in a brief note he slipped under her door.
reasons: Understanding happens privately in the mind, so it can't be a show put on for others.
Parading the paper so that every classmate has to see it is a deliberate display.
Quietly putting the result away shows modesty, not a wish to be admired.
A private note has no audience, so it can't be a showy performance.
